items.titleEn: VOO & Chill is gaining momentum: What comes next for the S&P 500?
items.summaryEn: Buy XLE as a tactical hedge against broad-index downside. The article notes energy has already sold off hard (Brent/WTI down >10% from highs). If crude stabilizes or rate-hike fears fade, energy often mean-reverts quickly versus the rest of the index. Key Risk: Crude keeps falling (another leg down in Brent/WTI), dragging XLE lower. Sell VOO (or SPY) into weakness. The article flags a double-top (716) with neckline near 689 and a likely retest toward 673 support. Pair that with macro risk: higher-for-longer rates (10Y ~5.0%) and slowing earnings growth. If AI and energy wobble, the broad index gets hit fast because tech is ~40% of the S&P 500.

items.titleEn: Micron, SanDisk stocks fall 3%: is Nvidia's crisis spreading to memory chips?
items.summaryEn: Buy MU. Nvidia leadership turmoil is a sentiment shock to AI supply chain, but Micron is the more direct beneficiary of any continued AI accelerator rollout because it supplies high-bandwidth memory (HBM) tied to next-gen AI chips. The article notes tight supply and rising prices, plus strong revenue growth and a clear near-term linkage to accelerator timing. If AI capex merely redistributes among memory suppliers, MU should hold up better than storage-focused peers. Key Risk: Cloud and data-center buyers actually pause or cut AI hardware orders, crushing HBM demand despite tight supply. Sell SNDK. The stock is more exposed to broader storage demand and timing, so Nvidia-specific disruption is less likely to be a direct tailwind. With the market already repricing AI supply-chain risk, SNDK’s rebound looks vulnerable to another cycle fear in NAND/SSD pricing even if memory supply remains tight. If AI spending shifts rather than expands, SNDK’s upside is capped while downside from sentiment and storage-cycle volatility is larger.

items.titleEn: Is Huang bigger than Nvidia? Susanna Streeter answers on ‘Zero Sum'
items.summaryEn: Buy SOXX (Semiconductor ETF). The scandal is likely to trigger short-term de-risking and export-policy headlines, but the second-order effect is that customers and governments push for “supply-chain certainty” and compliance tracking—favoring established US semiconductor suppliers and diversified exposure over single-company leadership risk. SOXX also spreads the leadership/geopolitical headline risk across many winners in the AI buildout. Key Risk: A sustained, tighter export regime that materially reduces addressable AI-chip demand for US semiconductor makers, overwhelming any compliance-driven capex shift. Sell NVDA. The news adds a direct leadership-confidence shock to the AI “picks-and-shovels” name, where a big chunk of the premium is tied to Jensen Huang personally. That raises the odds of multiple compression even if demand stays strong, because investors will demand proof of a broader leadership bench and cleaner governance while regulators and lawmakers tighten scrutiny around AI and chip exports.

items.titleEn: What next for Nvidia stock as board considers ousting Jensen Huang?
items.summaryEn: Buy NVDA put spreads (e.g., buy 1–3 month puts near $155 and sell lower-strike puts) into the next earnings catalyst. The stock is highly sensitive to both board action and earnings guidance; implied volatility should stay elevated, and downside skew is likely if guidance or China exposure headlines worsen. Key Risk: Earnings confirm strong growth and the board process calms down, causing a sharp rebound that crushes put value. Sell NVDA. The board ouster plan plus no succession plan is a direct hit to execution risk, and the stock is already in a technical downtrend below key support ($164) with heavy sentiment damage. Any CEO uncertainty will keep multiple compression pressure on a stock priced for flawless leadership.

items.titleEn: STOXX 600 hits record high: why are European stocks outperforming Wall Street?
items.summaryEn: Buy STOXX 600 exposure via an ETF like iShares STOXX Europe 600 UCITS (EXX1) but tilt to ex-energy names. The thesis is earnings-led upside: STOXX 600 is at record highs on upgraded guidance (Siemens, Merck) and lower oil is supporting margins and inflation expectations. The key is the index’s growth is real outside energy—energy’s 150%+ profit surge is the distortion, so you want the industrial/healthcare earnings engine, not the oil tailwind. Key Risk: Oil rebounds sharply, lifting inflation and crushing the margin/investor confidence benefit that’s driving the ex-energy earnings rerating. Buy Siemens (SIE.DE). It’s the cleanest “tangible earnings” winner in the article: raised comparable revenue growth target to 7%–11%, industrial profit up 22%, and orders up 58% to a record €34.77bn, including electrical infrastructure tied to data centers. This positions Siemens to benefit from AI capex indirectly (power, rail, industrial automation) without paying US tech valuation multiples.

items.titleEn: Who could potentially replace Jensen Huang if Nvidia ousts him?
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Chip giant Nvidia's board was reportedly meeting Wednesday to discuss the future of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang after he dated an accused Chinese spy, according to U.S. media. The 63-year-old tech titan, who has led the key AI giant since it was founded in 1993, has been beleaguered by reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a data center executive who has been accused by U.S. intelligence of working for China's Ministry of State Security.

items.titleEn: Nvidia stock crashes 8%, but why are AMD and Broadcom stocks rising?
items.summaryEn: Buy AMD (NASDAQ: AMD). Nvidia’s leadership uncertainty is a near-term sentiment shock that can temporarily slow AI infrastructure decisions, giving AMD a window to win incremental share with Instinct accelerators plus EPYC server CPUs. The market is already bidding AMD up after-hours, signaling investors expect customers to diversify away from a single supplier when risk rises. Key catalyst is Nvidia’s 17 Nov results: any sign of demand/margin resilience will stabilize the whole complex, while AMD keeps benefiting from “second-source” narratives. Key Risk: AMD fails to convert “diversification” into real AI accelerator wins (weak guidance or margin compression), so the stock pop fades. Buy Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO). Nvidia’s rivals don’t need to replace Nvidia chips one-for-one—networking and custom AI silicon design are where switching friction is lower. AVGO can gain as hyperscalers and large enterprises re-balance AI stacks and expand interconnect capacity, and its growth can rise even if workloads don’t fully migrate off Nvidia. The after-hours move suggests investors see AVGO as a beneficiary of broader AI build-out rather than a direct Nvidia substitute.

items.titleEn: Foxconn profit surges 34%, but Apple is no longer its biggest story
items.summaryEn: Buy Foxconn. Profit and revenue both surged (net profit +34%, revenue +47%), and AI infrastructure is now the core growth engine (cloud/networking already 51% of revenue in the prior quarter). The market is shifting from “iPhone assembler” to “AI server systems integrator,” and Foxconn’s vertical integration and localized production position it to keep winning AI rack/network work through 2027. Key Risk: AI server demand stays strong but Foxconn’s margins keep compressing fast (revenue grows faster than profit), wiping out the earnings upside. Buy Nvidia. Foxconn’s AI server ramp is ultimately powered by Nvidia compute and networking ecosystems; Foxconn is assembling AI racks and networking systems for major customers, which typically means higher Nvidia GPU utilization. If Foxconn’s AI infrastructure buildout is accelerating, Nvidia’s order flow and platform demand should benefit as customers expand training/inference capacity.

items.titleEn: Costco announces record $13.3 billion special dividend: is the stock a buy?
items.summaryEn: Buy COST. The $30 special dividend plus the renewed $4B buyback signals Costco’s cash engine is still throwing off more than it can reinvest at attractive returns. With operating cash flow of $15.83B and free cash flow of ~$9.39B, the payout looks like capital allocation, not financial stress. The stock is near highs, but the market is still underpricing the durability of member spending and the ability to keep returning cash while funding growth (warehouses + faster digital delivery). Key Risk: Membership growth or same-store sales slow enough that the premium valuation (about 46x earnings) can’t be justified, forcing future payouts to shrink. Sell COST short-term. The stock is already near its annual high and priced for dependable growth; the special dividend is a one-off cash return that the share price will largely offset on the ex-dividend mechanics. If the next catalysts (Nov sales on Dec 2, earnings Dec 10) don’t beat expectations, the premium multiple can compress quickly.
